root_cause_analysis.title: The brand's identity is stated inconsistently, which invites mistaken identity
root_cause_analysis.diagnosis: The site presents conflicting or under-specified versions of who it is - across its own name, its structured data, its contact details, or the attributes that would distinguish it from a similarly-named entity. Entity resolution fails by merging, so the practical outcome is not silence but an assistant confidently attributing another organisation's facts to this brand.
root_cause_analysis.why_it_matters: Misrepresentation is harder to detect and more damaging than absence, because nothing on the brand's own analytics shows it happening.
fix_order: Fix the canonical name string first - every other identity signal depends on it.
Publish one Organization node with a stable @id, complete attributes and sameAs links.
Make the contact and location facts identical everywhere they appear, on-site and on external profiles.

proactive_recommendations.title: Add question-shaped headings that answer real user questions
proactive_recommendations.rationale: No heading anywhere in the sample is phrased as a question, so the site's content is not organised around the questions people actually ask.
proactive_recommendations.mechanism: Retrieval matches a user's question against passages. A section headed with the question, answered in the first sentence beneath it, is the single highest-yield format for being selected and quoted - and it costs nothing beyond restructuring copy you already have.
steps: List the 10 questions your sales or support team answers most often.
Give each one an H2 phrased exactly as the question, with a direct answer in the first sentence and detail after it.
Where several belong together, group them on one page and mark that page up as FAQPage.
Keep each answer self-contained so a quote of it remains accurate out of context.

proactive_recommendations.title: Publish an llms.txt context file at the site root
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site has no /llms.txt. This is an emerging convention rather than a standard, so its absence is not a defect - but it is a cheap way to tell an LLM fetcher which pages carry the authoritative facts.
proactive_recommendations.mechanism: An assistant fetching a site under time pressure picks a small number of URLs. A short Markdown index at a predictable path lets you nominate which ones - your canonical product, pricing, about and documentation pages - rather than leaving the choice to whatever the crawler happened to reach.
steps: Create /llms.txt as Markdown: an H1 with the organisation name, a one-line blockquote summary, then linked sections for the pages that hold the authoritative facts.
Keep it short and link only to canonical URLs.
Serve it as text/plain or text/markdown and regenerate it when the information architecture changes.

proactive_recommendations.title: Publish a feed so updates are discovered without a re-crawl
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site publishes editorial content but exposes no RSS/Atom/JSON feed.
proactive_recommendations.mechanism: A feed is a push-shaped discovery channel: aggregators, newsletters and several retrieval pipelines poll it and pick up new articles within hours instead of waiting for the next crawl of an index page. It also gives every item an unambiguous date.
proactive_recommendations.evidence: 1 editorial page(s) sampled; no feed link found in any <head>.
steps: Generate an RSS or JSON feed of the most recent items with title, link, summary and publication date.
Advertise it with `<link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml">` in the head of the section index.
